newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money traded at 5.5/6.0 percent.

text.p: Indonesia's call money rate was at 5.5/6.0 percent on Monday on sustained ample liquidity.
Dealers said liquidity was still flush, aided by early central bank injection of some 867 billion rupiah.
"There is no other major issue. Liquidity just remains ample," one state bank dealer said.
Some dealers seemed to view the sustained ample conditions as the central bank's signal to curb offhore inflows.
"Some are not so worried yet as they can adjust slowly to meet the new reserve requirement rate effective from April 16," one local bank dealer.
"But banks might have to interpret the signals differently if liquidity continues to be ample beyond April," he added.
One-month money was at 11.50/11.75 percent and three-month was at 12.75/13.00 percent. Dealers said one-month money was well offered.
The central bank did not offer overnight bilateral papers (SBIs). It only offered seven-day SBIs at 6.5 percent, 14-day at 8.5 percent and one-month at 10.75 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 6.6 percent, compared with 4.59 percent on Thursday.
Bond dealers said demand increased as several mutual funds with focus on investments in bonds were set up recently.
One major dealer said prices edged up between 25 and 50 basis points on Monday, driving their yields down slightly.
But the yield of the benchmark PLN V/A bond was still at 15.37 percent at the price of 105.25 percent.
